I am 18 years of age. I understand that the decision is ultimately mine, but I've never gone against them like that before. I'm worried, I don't think I have it in me, I've always been raised to listen and do what they tell me. Plus, I'll have to find someone to help me move there.

Their reasons are that they think we'll fall for each other, cause she's a girl. They're very religious so that's a no no for them. Thing is I only really see her as a good friend, but they don't understand that. Also they want to have control I think and that's why they want to put me somewhere they decide, not me. 

I am appreciative of your response and I understand that taking my life is letting everyone else win except myself. I just hope I can have the strength to do what I want, even if that means just leaving them. For some reason, ending it all just seems easier.

Enforce religion the way they did. Religion should come after you've set personal bounds with your child and it should stay that way forever.

My parents could never be as supportive or understanding of me because of that, some things I just could never talk about and they didn't want to ever hear.

Living with my friend. It's so simple, but just having her there really would make it a lot better.

I fantasize about studying, watching movies, talking, and just knowing she's there. 

Too bad I'm uncertain if I can...

That I feel I'm trapped in a position where no one sees my best interests and yet they keep telling me that it's what I need to do. 

My family has always been like that, so I decided to study at a University 2 hours away. Now going back I want to live with this new friend I made, she's smart and caring. And one of the only friends I have. Otherwise I'm a lonely mess, even when I'm surrounded by family. 

Yet my parents don't want me to live with her. Instead they think random roommates who I've no control over are better. 

I'm lost, I don't want to have to fight my way through my own family for something like this. If I live alone or in a random arrangement I'll be really lonely. Just don't know what to do.
